scopeNote: Each research question keeps its own computational model and assumptions. The linked source states the question or supplies the unresolved bounds gap; this review does not certify an exhaustive search.

matching.title: How many passes does near-optimal matching need?
matching.setup: Unweighted bipartite matching · insertion-only streams · O(n polylog n) bits · output matching edges
matching.question: What is the optimal dependence on ε of the number of passes needed to return a (1−ε)-approximate maximum matching?
matching.context: The reviewed landscape has O(1/ε²) passes for algorithms whose pass bound is independent of n, versus an Ω(log(1/ε)) lower bound for sufficiently small fixed ε. Closing this gap could improve either side.
matching.status: Open direction inferred from a reviewed bounds gap · lower-bound source is a preprint

weighted_matching.title: How much weight can linear-in-1/p queries preserve?
weighted_matching.setup: Edge-weighted stochastic matching · independent edge survival · non-adaptive queries · p = min pₑ
weighted_matching.question: Can a subgraph of maximum degree O(1/p) preserve more of the expected optimum matching weight? What is the best approximation in this query regime?
weighted_matching.context: Derakhshan–Saneian obtain retained-weight fractions 0.68 on general graphs and 0.73 on bipartite graphs. Their question fixes the linear dependence on 1/p; allowing a larger polynomial or exponential dependence is a different regime.
weighted_matching.status: Question posed in the cited paper; scope checked against the atlas review

mis.title: Can general-graph MIS beat logarithmic rounds?
mis.setup: Maximal independent set · classical randomized LOCAL · general graphs · all vertices finish with high probability
mis.question: Is there an o(log n)-round randomized LOCAL algorithm for maximal independent set on every n-vertex graph?
mis.context: Khoury–Schild achieve sublogarithmic rounds when there are no cycles of length at most six. They explicitly leave the general-graph question open. The resource here is elapsed rounds, not awake rounds or local probe count.
mis.status: Open Question 1 in the cited paper

cc.title: Can the cluster-LP gap reach 4/3?
cc.setup: Correlation clustering · complete unweighted signed graphs · minimize disagreements · cluster LP
cc.question: Can every feasible cluster-LP solution be rounded with approximation factor 4/3, or is its integrality gap strictly larger?
cc.context: The reviewed 2026 preprint places the gap between 4/3 and 1.3865. This concerns the LP relaxation: 4/3 is not a hardness threshold for all algorithms, nor a bound for maximizing agreements.
cc.status: Open direction inferred from the cited integrality-gap bounds · preprint

edge.title: Fewer colors with little recoloring
edge.setup: Fully dynamic proper edge coloring · simple graphs · Δ+C colors · recourse counts recolored edges
edge.question: Can shift-tree methods maintain low recoloring recourse with a much smaller extra palette C, especially when C is constant?
edge.context: Sadeh–Kaplan obtain tight recourse for large extra palettes and identify smaller palettes as a next step. They also ask how to reduce update time while retaining low recourse; the two costs must remain distinct.
edge.status: Question posed in Section 3 of the cited preprint

vertex.title: Beyond √n for adaptive dynamic coloring
vertex.setup: Fully dynamic (Δ+1)-vertex coloring · adaptive adversary · general graphs · update time
vertex.question: Can adaptive dynamic (Δ+1)-coloring achieve update time below the √n scale, or can a nontrivial lower bound explain the barrier?
vertex.context: Gil–Halldórsson give Õ(√n) worst-case update time and at most three recolorings. They identify faster algorithms or lower bounds as open directions. Their discussion of random color trials is a technique limitation, not a lower bound for the problem.
vertex.status: Question posed in the cited preprint, accepted to SODA 2027

weighted_matching:dynamic.title: Can near-optimal matching be maintained in polylogarithmic time?
weighted_matching:dynamic.question: Can a fully dynamic algorithm maintain an explicit (1−ε)-approximate maximum-weight matching with update time polynomial in log n and 1/ε?
weighted_matching:dynamic.setup: General graphs · positive edge weights with polynomial aspect ratio · edge insertions and deletions · explicit matching edges
weighted_matching:dynamic.context: The displayed near-optimal algorithms still depend polynomially on graph size. Value-only estimates and partially dynamic updates are different contracts.
weighted_matching:dynamic.status: Open direction identified in the cited preprints; stronger polynomial dependence on 1/ε is the target stated here.
